text:
incident-bot: ⚠️ Pager: Dedicated pool dp-eu-west-1 experiencing sustained token latency spike and 502s starting 03/12 11:29 UTC. Error rate > 8% (5m), p95 latency 2.3s, throughput near reserved throughput. Potential customer impact: several customers reporting higher error rates and slow responses. Alert ID: PAG-20260312-0482

maya: oncall — maya here. seeing the alert in datadog. i'm going to try burst-capacity toggle + temporary traffic-shaping. tagging @autoscale-bot and @ben_sre for visibility.

autoscale-bot: autoscale-bot: Received request to modify pool dp-eu-west-1. Current state: autoscaling=on, burst=disabled, capacity=reserved(32xA100). Estimated headroom if burst enabled: ~2.0x for 20m.

maya: plan: 1) enable burst capacity (2x) for dp-eu-west-1 2) reduce non-critical tenant quotas (free/dev) by 60% for 15m 3) disable non-essential features that add tail latency (streaming & live-tooling) for Dedicated in eu-west 4) monitor error rates and latency, roll back if errors increase.

maya: executing burst enable now. command: ```
redwoodctl dedicated update-pool --pool-id dp-eu-west-1 \
  --burst-enabled true \
  --burst-multiplier 2 \
  --burst-duration 20m
```

autoscale-bot: autoscale-bot: burst enable accepted for dp-eu-west-1. New target headroom ~2.0x. Expected steady-state within 40s.

ben_sre: i see the write in control plane. good call. maya, can you also temporarily increase the scaling cooldown to 45s to avoid oscillation? run: ```
redwoodctl dedicated update-pool --pool-id dp-eu-west-1 --scaling-cooldown 45s
```

maya: doing cooldown update now. executed. also applying quota changes for dev/free tenants to free up tokens. patch: ```
redwoodctl quotas batch-update --selector "tier:free OR tier:dev" \
  --qps-multiplier 0.4 --duration 15m
```

incident-bot: Note: quota change applied. 312 tenants affected. Monitoring eviction rate.

leah_support: support team — we have 4 active customer tickets reporting 502s; i drafted an update to send to impacted customers. preview: "We are experiencing elevated latency and intermittent errors for dedicated workloads in eu-west. We have enabled temporary burst capacity and applied traffic shaping to restore service. Engineers are monitoring; expected resolution within 30 minutes." ok to send?

ryan_prodeng: +1 on that message. add that we are prioritizing paid customers and that canary-internal telemetry looks good after burst. keep it brief.

maya: thumbs up. leah, send that message and include link to status page. i've been watching metrics: error rate dropped from 8.3% -> 2.1% over the last 3 minutes post-burst; p95 latency from 2.3s -> 1.1s. throughput increased ~1.9x. continuing to observe.

tom_plat: question: do we need to disable streaming as well, or just deprioritize it? streaming uses more persistent connections and increases KV cache churn.

maya: disabling streaming for Dedicated in eu-west for 15m. command: ```
redwoodctl feature toggle --region eu-west --scope dedicated --feature streaming --state off --expires 15m
```

autoscale-bot: autoscale-bot: feature toggle applied. streaming disabled for dedicated eu-west.

ben_sre: monitoring looks stable. small note: keep an eye on prefix-cache hit rate — it can regress if we drastically change tenant routing.

maya: watching cache hit rate. it's holding ~82% (was 88%). acceptable tradeoff for now. if hit rate drops below 70% rollback burst.

ben_sre: agree. i'll take a full postmortem if anything else happens. i'm on call for the next 45m so i'll take the handoff once maya steps out.

maya: handoff plan for @ben_sre in 30m: summary + artifacts: runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-traffic|runbook>, dashboard: <https://grafana.redwood/internal/dp-eu-west-1|grafana>, logs query: ```
index:dedicated_eu-west-1 error=502 | stats count by tenant_tier
```

leah_support: update sent to impacted customers. included note about prioritization and expected timeframe.

maya: current status: burst enabled, cooldown increased, streaming disabled, quotas reduced for non-paid tiers. metrics: errors 2.0%, p95 1.05s, cpu util 68%. keeping this thread active. will escalate to infra if errors climb back above 5% or latency p95 >1.8s.

ben_sre: i'll be online and monitoring. if situation stabilizes for 40m we'll start rolling back in this order: 1) restore quotas 2) re-enable streaming 3) disable burst. rollback commands are mirror of above.

incident-bot: Incident note: mitigation actions taken and customer notifications sent. Close criteria: <=1% errors for 15m and stable latency.

maya: thanks team. i'll ping again at handoff or earlier if anything changes. :white_check_mark:
